name: pstack-claude
description: Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, DeepSeek Harness, Gemini, Grok Build, Kimi Code, MiniMax Code, Muse, OMP, OpenCode, Pi, Prime Agent, etc versions of Poteto's pstack. Rigorous agent workflows with Cursor primitives translated for other harnesses.

# pstack Lauren Tan's [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in [`tools/forks.json`](tools/forks.json). Tell `poteto-mode` your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified. For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, `/create-formal-verification-skill` picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate [agent-formal-verify](https://github.com/michael-denyer/agent-formal-verify) plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust. ## Built for Claude Code This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. [Upstream's Claude Code install](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/0b46ec3/harness/pstack/claude-code) asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to `poteto-mode`. ## Install ### Any harness: npm or Homebrew ```shell npx open-pstack ``` Or install it once and run it by name: ```shell npm install -g open-pstack open-pstack ``` With Homebrew: ```shell brew install michael-denyer/tap/open-pstack ``` `open-pstack` needs Node 20 or later; Homebrew installs Node for you. It finds the agent harnesses on your `PATH` and shows a picker. Press Enter to install into the ones it found, or choose others by number or id, then confirm the planned steps. It runs the same recipe as each harness's section below. | Option | Effect | | --- | --- | | `--only claude,pi` | Install into the named harnesses without the picker. Each section below gives its id. | | `--yes` | Install into every detected harness without asking. | | `--dry-run` | Print every step without running or writing anything. | | `--list` | Show each harness id and whether it was detected. | The shared `~/.agents/skills` directory (id `skills`) is never chosen by default, because Codex and OpenCode read it as well as their own plugin and would load each skill twice. Choose it for Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, or DeepSeek Harness. Muse, Grok Build, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, and the shared skills directory install from a local copy of the plugin, so no clone is needed: `open-pstack` stages the copy that ships with it at `~/.local/share/open-pstack/pstack`, or under `XDG_DATA_HOME` when that is set. To update, upgrade the installer (`npm update -g open-pstack` or `brew upgrade open-pstack`) and run `open-pstack` again. That refreshes the staged copy, so the shared skills links pick up the new version and any new skills. Plugins that a harness installed itself update through that harness, as its section below describes. See [Install with open-pstack](docs/reference.md#install-with-open-pstack) for uninstalling. ### One harness at a time
Claude Code Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: ```text /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run `/plugin`, open the **Marketplaces** tab, select `pstack-claude`, and choose **Enable auto-update**. To update once by hand, run `claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude`. Or: `npx open-pstack --only claude`.
Codex Run in your terminal: ```shell codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude ``` Invoke a skill by typing `$` and its name, such as `$poteto-mode` or `$babysit`, then choosing its entry, which inserts `$pstack:`. `/skills` lists every skill. Or: `npx open-pstack --only codex`.
Pi Run in your terminal, with Pi 1.5.1 or later: ```shell pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude ``` The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus `/loop` and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with `/skill:`. Or: `npx open-pstack --only pi`.
GitHub Copilot Run in your terminal: ```shell copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share `~/.copilot`. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs `setup-pstack` to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice. The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, `setup-pstack` offers a [standing instruction](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/copilot.md#wire-it-in) for `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, `copilot -p` sessions list no plugin skills and a `skill` call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected. Or: `npx open-pstack --only copilot`.
Muse Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack muse plugins approve pstack ``` The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its `SessionStart` hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with `/` (for example `/poteto-mode`), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only muse`.
OMP Run in your terminal: ```shell omp plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude omp plugin install --scope user pstack@pstack-claude ``` Restart OMP after installing, disabling, or uninstalling pstack. OMP 18.16.0 shares one plugin cache across scopes, so an upgrade or removal can affect other installations; inspect their source and scope before changing them. See [OMP issue 16827](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/issues/16827). Or: `npx open-pstack --only omp`.
Kimi Code CLI After a release containing `kimi.plugin.json` is published, close other Kimi sessions and install it in a fresh Kimi Code CLI session: ```text /plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude /reload ``` To test an unreleased checkout, use `/plugins install /absolute/path/to/pstack-claude` instead, followed by `/reload`; Kimi copies the whole checkout, including Git metadata and local files, so use a clean, reviewed copy. To update, close other Kimi sessions, reinstall from the same source in a fresh session, and run `/reload`. Invoke a skill as `/skill:pstack:poteto-mode`; see the [Kimi mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/kimi-tools.md) for tool guidance. `open-pstack --only kimi` prints these steps; Kimi installs plugins only from inside a session.
Grok Build ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude grok plugin install "$PWD/plugins/pstack" --trust grok plugin enable pstack ``` Start a new session and use `/poteto-mode` to load the skill explicitly. To update a local install, quit Grok sessions, inspect `grok plugin details pstack` and back up any edits in the installed copy, pull the checkout, run `grok plugin uninstall pstack --keep-data`, and repeat the last two commands. If pstack was disabled, disable it again before restarting. `grok plugin update` does not refresh a local install. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only grok`.
MiniMax Code For a first install, check that `${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack` does not already exist. Then run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins" cp -R plugins/pstack "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack" ``` MiniMax Code loads each directory under `plugins/` in its data directory as a local plugin, and reads pstack through its Claude Code reader with the skills, agents, and routing hook. `mcode plugin list` shows it as `pstack@local`. To update, record its enabled state, quit every `mcode` process, and move `plugins/pstack` to an unused path outside `plugins/`. Run `git pull` and the `cp` line again. Check `mcode plugin list` and restore the previous enabled state if needed. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only minimax`.
OpenCode 2 Clone the repository, then add the absolute path to `plugins/pstack/opencode` to the existing `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. On Windows, use a path such as `C:/Users/name/pstack-claude/plugins/pstack/opencode`. Restart OpenCode after checkout updates. Alternatively, install, check, or update the native Git package: ```bash opencode plugin add 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' opencode plugin check 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' opencode plugin update 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main' ``` A commit-pinned reference does not advance. If a check immediately after installation reports no package plugins, wait for the server to load it and check again. If you previously installed pstack skills into `~/.agents/skills`, inspect the links and remove only those pointing to your pstack checkout before using the plugin. The plugin registers `pstack-` skill IDs, registers the bundled agents as subagents under their Claude Code names, such as `pstack:poteto-agent`, and adds routing in root sessions. If routing is missing, run `opencode api get /api/skill` and check that each `pstack-` path belongs to this plugin. Resolve any conflicting skill before manually invoking that ID. Use `session hook: off` in the OpenCode model sheet to disable routing. To remove the plugin, remove its configured path and restart the service, or use `opencode plugin remove` with the exact Git specifier. OpenCode 1 is unsupported. See the [OpenCode mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/opencode-tools.md). Or: `npx open-pstack --only opencode`.
Antigravity (agy) Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack ``` This installs the native Antigravity plugin bundle (`skills`, `agents`, and `SessionStart` routing hook) into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/pstack`. Or, without a clone: `npx open-pstack --only agy`.
DeepSeek Harness (skills-only) Use the [shared skills installation](#other-harnesses) below to link each pstack skill directory into `~/.agents/skills/`, which DSH discovers by default. Ask for `poteto-mode` by name and use the [DSH mapping](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/dsh-tools.md), regardless of the model provider. On Windows, `open-pstack` launches a harness installed as a `.cmd` or `.bat` shim through `cmd.exe`. It wrapped each argument in double quotes, which leave `%NAME%` open to expansion, so a staged plugin path that named a defined variable, such as one under a data directory with `%SystemRoot%` in its name, reached the harness changed. Each argument and the shim's own path are now caret-escaped for `cmd.exe`. The Windows installer job proves this with such a path, with stubs in a directory whose name has a space and `&`, and with a stub that reads `%~1` instead of forwarding `%*` ([#526](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/526)).

In a Claude Code cloud session, whose GitHub proxy refuses GraphQL, `watch-pr` now reads the PR over REST instead of stopping with exit 7. At the first refusal it switches, for the rest of the run, to a reader that gets the PR's facts from `pulls/<pr>`, its review threads from the proxy's `ccr/review_threads` route, and its checks from the head's check runs and statuses. The checks are de-duplicated as `gh pr checks` does: the newest run for each name, workflow, and event. Runs of Copilot's review agent are left out, as GitHub's rollup le

On Pi, a `pi agent host: hc` line in a sheet committed with the project now applies, for worktree agents too. The extension read that line only from the agent directory's sheet, while the prompt sheet and model routing already read the committed one. A project's committed sheet now replaces the agent directory's sheet for this line as well, so in a project whose sheet has no `pi agent host: hc` line, agents run as RPC children even when the agent directory's sheet sets it. The extension also asks git for a directory's root once per process instead of on every agent start and every subagent spawn (12.6 ms each on macOS). [`docs/pi-equivalence.md`](docs/pi-equivalence.md) row H07 says that `pi agent tools: off` and `pi ask tool: off` are read at install, from the directory Pi started in, because Pi registers tools before any session directory is known ([#512](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/512)).

The OpenCode 2 plugin now registers the four bundled agents as subagents under their Claude Code names, such as `pstack:poteto-agent`, so a skill's `subagent_type` names an OpenCode agent as written, without entries in `opencode.json`. OpenCode's agent editor has no

A Claude Code cloud session refuses GitHub GraphQL, so `gh pr checks`, `gh pr merge`, `ship-pr`, and `watch-pr` fail there. When `gh pr checks` fails with that refusal, `fix-ci` now reads the head's check runs and commit statuses over REST, and treats the two together as the source of truth. When the watcher or `ship-pr inspect` reports the refusal, the shipping playbook stops at merge-ready and reports the limit. [`cloud-session-pr-reads.md`](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/references/cloud-session-pr-reads.md) gains the reads for an Actions run's jobs, one job's log, and `gh run view` and `gh run list`. It also says how a check run's `status` and `conclusion` give its result. The check-runs and jobs reads still return only the first 30 rows ([#516](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/516)). From @abc123931 ([#515](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/515), part of [#494](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/494)).

Since 0.9.146, the override sheet that `setup-pstack` writes, and its steps 4 and 8, said `PSTACK_SESSION_HOOK=off` keeps the routing hook off on every runtime. Only the shared session hook reads the variable: on Claude Code, and on Codex, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and Antigravity when the runtime passes it to its hooks. MiniMax Code withholds it from its hooks, and the OMP, OpenCode, and Pi plugins read only the sheet, so on those runtimes the sheet and the agent named an override that does nothing. The sheet and both steps now name the runtimes. This is also the first `open-pstack` release published to npm through trusted publishing. From @flipcyde101 ([#499](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/499), for [#495](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/495)).

`open-pstack` installs pstack from npm (`npx open-pstack`) or Homebrew (`brew install michael-denyer/tap/open-pstack`). It lists the agent harnesses on `PATH`, lets you pick, and runs each harness's README recipe. `--only`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, and `--list` cover scripted use. Muse, Grok Build, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, and the shared `~/.agents/skills` directory install from the plugin copy it ships, staged at `~/.local/share/open-pstack/pstack`, so they no longer need a clone. The shared skills directory is never chosen by default, because Codex and OpenCode read it as well as their own plugin. Pushing a release tag publishes the npm package with provenance through trusted publishing. A rerun on Codex, Copilot, OMP, Muse, Grok, or Antigravity is untested ([#508](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/508)), and so is the Windows path ([#509](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/509)) ([#510](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/510)).

The Pi extension now reads a project's committed `.claude/pstack-models.md`, the same file the Claude Code session hook reads, and it replaces the user's sheet in that project as it does on Claud

pstack

Lauren Tan's pstack is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in tools/forks.json.

Tell poteto-mode your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified.

For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, /create-formal-verification-skill picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate agent-formal-verify plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust.

Built for Claude Code

This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. Upstream's Claude Code install asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to poteto-mode.

Install

Any harness: npm or Homebrew

npx open-pstack

Or install it once and run it by name:

npm install -g open-pstack
open-pstack

With Homebrew:

brew install michael-denyer/tap/open-pstack

open-pstack needs Node 20 or later; Homebrew installs Node for you. It finds the agent harnesses on your PATH and shows a picker. Press Enter to install into the ones it found, or choose others by number or id, then confirm the planned steps. It runs the same recipe as each harness's section below.

Option Effect
--only claude,pi Install into the named harnesses without the picker. Each section below gives its id.
--yes Install into every detected harness without asking.
--dry-run Print every step without running or writing anything.
--list Show each harness id and whether it was detected.

The shared ~/.agents/skills directory (id skills) is never chosen by default, because Codex and OpenCode read it as well as their own plugin and would load each skill twice. Choose it for Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, or DeepSeek Harness.

Muse, Grok Build, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, and the shared skills directory install from a local copy of the plugin, so no clone is needed: open-pstack stages the copy that ships with it at ~/.local/share/open-pstack/pstack, or under XDG_DATA_HOME when that is set. To update, upgrade the installer (npm update -g open-pstack or brew upgrade open-pstack) and run open-pstack again. That refreshes the staged copy, so the shared skills links pick up the new version and any new skills. Plugins that a harness installed itself update through that harness, as its section below describes. See Install with open-pstack for uninstalling.

One harness at a time

Claude Code

Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later:

/plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
/plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run /plugin, open the Marketplaces tab, select pstack-claude, and choose Enable auto-update. To update once by hand, run claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude.

Or: npx open-pstack --only claude.

Codex

Run in your terminal:

codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude

Invoke a skill by typing $ and its name, such as $poteto-mode or $babysit, then choosing its entry, which inserts $pstack:<name>. /skills lists every skill.

Or: npx open-pstack --only codex.

Pi

Run in your terminal, with Pi 1.5.1 or later:

pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude

The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus /loop and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with /skill:<name>.

Or: npx open-pstack --only pi.

GitHub Copilot

Run in your terminal:

copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share ~/.copilot. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs setup-pstack to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice.

The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, setup-pstack offers a standing instruction for ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, copilot -p sessions list no plugin skills and a skill call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.

Or: npx open-pstack --only copilot.

Muse

Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack
muse plugins approve pstack

The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its SessionStart hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with /<name> (for example /poteto-mode), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill.

Or, without a clone: npx open-pstack --only muse.

OMP

Run in your terminal:

omp plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
omp plugin install --scope user pstack@pstack-claude

Restart OMP after installing, disabling, or uninstalling pstack. OMP 18.16.0 shares one plugin cache across scopes, so an upgrade or removal can affect other installations; inspect their source and scope before changing them. See OMP issue 16827.

Or: npx open-pstack --only omp.

Kimi Code CLI

After a release containing kimi.plugin.json is published, close other Kimi sessions and install it in a fresh Kimi Code CLI session:

/plugins install https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
/reload

To test an unreleased checkout, use /plugins install /absolute/path/to/pstack-claude instead, followed by /reload; Kimi copies the whole checkout, including Git metadata and local files, so use a clean, reviewed copy. To update, close other Kimi sessions, reinstall from the same source in a fresh session, and run /reload. Invoke a skill as /skill:pstack:poteto-mode; see the Kimi mapping for tool guidance.

open-pstack --only kimi prints these steps; Kimi installs plugins only from inside a session.

Grok Build 
git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
grok plugin install "$PWD/plugins/pstack" --trust
grok plugin enable pstack

Start a new session and use /poteto-mode to load the skill explicitly. To update a local install, quit Grok sessions, inspect grok plugin details pstack and back up any edits in the installed copy, pull the checkout, run grok plugin uninstall pstack --keep-data, and repeat the last two commands. If pstack was disabled, disable it again before restarting. grok plugin update does not refresh a local install.

Or, without a clone: npx open-pstack --only grok.

MiniMax Code

For a first install, check that ${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack does not already exist. Then run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
mkdir -p "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins"
cp -R plugins/pstack "${MINIMAX_DATA_DIR:-$HOME/.minimax}/plugins/pstack"

MiniMax Code loads each directory under plugins/ in its data directory as a local plugin, and reads pstack through its Claude Code reader with the skills, agents, and routing hook. mcode plugin list shows it as pstack@local. To update, record its enabled state, quit every mcode process, and move plugins/pstack to an unused path outside plugins/. Run git pull and the cp line again. Check mcode plugin list and restore the previous enabled state if needed.

Or, without a clone: npx open-pstack --only minimax.

OpenCode 2

Clone the repository, then add the absolute path to plugins/pstack/opencode to the existing plugins array in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc. On Windows, use a path such as C:/Users/name/pstack-claude/plugins/pstack/opencode. Restart OpenCode after checkout updates.

Alternatively, install, check, or update the native Git package:

opencode plugin add 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main'
opencode plugin check 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main'
opencode plugin update 'github:michael-denyer/pstack-claude#main'

A commit-pinned reference does not advance. If a check immediately after installation reports no package plugins, wait for the server to load it and check again.

If you previously installed pstack skills into ~/.agents/skills, inspect the links and remove only those pointing to your pstack checkout before using the plugin.

The plugin registers pstack- skill IDs, registers the bundled agents as subagents under their Claude Code names, such as pstack:poteto-agent, and adds routing in root sessions. If routing is missing, run opencode api get /api/skill and check that each pstack- path belongs to this plugin. Resolve any conflicting skill before manually invoking that ID. Use session hook: off in the OpenCode model sheet to disable routing. To remove the plugin, remove its configured path and restart the service, or use opencode plugin remove with the exact Git specifier. OpenCode 1 is unsupported. See the OpenCode mapping.

Or: npx open-pstack --only opencode.

Antigravity (agy)

Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
agy plugin install ./plugins/pstack

This installs the native Antigravity plugin bundle (skills, agents, and SessionStart routing hook) into ~/.gemini/config/plugins/pstack.

Or, without a clone: npx open-pstack --only agy.

DeepSeek Harness (skills-only)

Use the shared skills installation below to link each pstack skill directory into ~/.agents/skills/, which DSH discovers by default. Ask for poteto-mode by name and use the DSH mapping, regardless of the model provider. This skills-only installation adds no native DSH bundle, Pi extension, routing hook, or role sheet.

Or, without a clone: npx open-pstack --only skills.

Other harnesses

Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, DeepSeek Harness skills-only installs, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from ~/.agents/skills/. Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do
  target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")"
  test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target"
done

To update, run git pull in the clone, then run the for loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for poteto-mode by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See shared installation for per-harness notes and uninstalling.

Or, without a clone: npx open-pstack --only skills.

Configure

pstack provides automatic routing on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Muse, MiniMax Code, Antigravity, Pi, Kimi Code CLI, OMP, and OpenCode 2. The runtimes deliver the instruction at different points: Kimi adds it while the plugin is enabled, OMP adds it before each main-agent turn, and OpenCode adds it at each model step in root sessions. Grok Build exposes a routing hint through a skill description; the model may not follow it. Codex requires hook trust through /hooks, and Muse requires muse plugins approve pstack. Other harnesses have no automatic routing.

Run setup-pstack to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max). On OMP, the session hook setting applies globally across profiles; on Kimi, enable or disable the plugin to control routing. See the routing reference.

Getting started

Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages.

For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses how and why to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in architect before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence.

A localized bug with a demonstrated cause can use the focused-fix exception. One delegate investigates and implements the correction when it preserves existing interfaces and state semantics and has a focused regression check. Reproduction, verification, and required independent review still apply; a small patch alone does not qualify.

Other playbooks cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects.

Details

  • Skills and slash commands
  • Runtime setup
  • Models and dependencies
  • Maintenance and port scope

Data handling

pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login.

This port has no automatic agent-diary reporting or diary opt-in setting. For a local decision trail, ask for show-me-your-work. Longer or unattended workflows also invoke it. The trail stays uncommitted by default. If the trail is committed and pushed to a shared PR, anyone with access to the PR can read it.

To share feedback, submit a short, manually reviewed report through GitHub issues. Include the pstack version, runtime, relevant workflow, and observed result. Remove credentials, customer data, private repository links, and sensitive log or configuration values before posting; share a summary instead of raw transcripts.

Contributing

Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md.

To support maintenance of this port, buy the maintainer a coffee.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An opinionated agent skill stack for Claude Code and Codex to improve autonomous workflows.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Pstack is a specialized plugin and skill stack designed to enhance the capabilities of AI coding harnesses like Claude Code and Codex. It ports rigorous, verified agent workflows originally designed for Cursor into other terminal-based AI environments. The tool manages named policy forks to enforce concise, simple, and secure coding practices during autonomous generation. By invoking specific workflows based on user goals, it significantly improves the reliability and outcome of agent-driven development tasks.
keyFeatures: Workflow translation: Ports Cursor-specific agent primitives to work seamlessly with Claude Code and Codex.
Policy management: Maintains named policy forks to enforce strict coding standards and behaviors.
Goal-oriented execution: Automatically invokes the correct operational workflow based on the stated task goal.
Code verification: Integrates strategies to ensure AI-generated code remains concise, simple, and secure.
Multi-harness support: Designed to operate across various agent environments including Pi and OpenCode.
